payload.claim: The four witnesses (test_a_push_that_never_returns_is_refused_within_the_limit, test_a_timed_out_push_leaves_no_process_behind, test_an_interrupted_push_leaves_no_process_behind, test_a_push_asks_ssh_for_keepalive_only_where_the_host_names_no_ssh_command) all depend on wall-clock timing (0.1s heartbeat files, a 2-second patched PUSH_TIMEOUT_S, a SIGALRM fired at 2.5s, a 1-second flat-count check, a sub-5-second refusal bound) and on process-group/signal semantics, which is inherently more flake-prone under host load than ordinary unit tests. With max_attempts: 3 and budget_usd: 62, a cell that hits timing flakiness on a loaded host has little room to recover. An operator should decide whether this budget and attempt count are adequate given that the entire acceptance surface is timing-based.
